# ElizaOS Developer Update (2026-08-03 → 2026-08-09)

This update summarizes merged work and high-signal open items across `elizaos/eliza` for the week, plus relevant Discord technical threads.

---

## 1) Core Framework

### Production promotion: `develop` → `main` (Cloud + Pages release)
The production release promotion landed as **[#17865](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17865)**, shipping a large batch of runtime + Cloud fixes and restoring the certification chain used to gate releases.

Key runtime-impacting payloads in/around this release:
- **Provider deadlines made cancellation-safe** (prevents “timeout cached as empty context” class) via **[#17490](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17490)**.
- **Planner loop reliability** improvements for reasoning models (tool-call starvation + retry widening) via **[#17630](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17630)**.
- **Turn delivery hygiene** (delivery floor, idempotent silence, verify-retry tolerances) via **[#17631](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17631)**.
- **Security envelope hardening**: avoid echoing untrusted external-content wrappers back into actions/tools via **[#17629](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17629)**.

### Runtime behavior: tighter engagement routing + addressed-to semantics
Several fixes tightened when the runtime should engage and what surfaces are treated as “direct”:
- **Extend addressed-to gate from tool promotion to full engagement routing**: **[#18174](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18174)** (reduces unprompted bot chatter in group contexts).
- **Private voice DMs now treated like text DMs** (direct-response grammar parity): **[#17863](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17863)**.
- **Voice-specific filler suppression on tool turns** (voice no longer speaks “On it…” during async tool work): **[#17810](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17810)**.

### Cloud runtime integrity: A2A trust boundary hardened
- **Reject caller-authored `system` messages at A2A boundary** (fail before billing/provider dispatch): **[#17643](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17643)**.

### CI/runtime standardization
- **Unified Bun runtime pin** (cross-repo alignment) referenced in weekly summary: **Bun `1.3.14`** via **[#17044](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17044)** and follow-ups (e.g. **[#17653](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17653)** for Windows gate pinning).
- Develop workflow/certification chain repairs and evidence robustness improvements shipped in multiple PRs (notably **[#17790](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17790)**, **[#17792](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17792)**, **[#17794](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17794)**, **[#17796](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17796)**, **[#17797](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17797)**, **[#17798](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17798)**, **[#17799](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17799)**, **[#17802](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17802)**).

---

## 2) New Features

### App-mode onboarding on `app.elizacloud.ai`
**[#17752](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17752)** introduces **app-mode**: when users log in on the app host, they are routed directly into *their dedicated agent* (auto entry/chooser/resume/fallback), instead of seeing the marketing surface.

**Developer implications**
- Hostname now matters: the UI can branch behavior based on app vs apex host.
- A guard ensures the expected host-mode is enforced (and tested) so deploys don’t silently drift.

### Cross-origin SSO Bridge (Dashboard ↔ App)
**[#17788](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17788)** adds an SSO bridge that supports “login once” across `app.elizacloud.ai` and other Cloud surfaces, using **atomic single-use codes stored in Postgres**, PKCE binding, and “fail-closed logout” semantics.

Minimal integration sketch (browser-side):
```ts
// Pseudocode: initiate SSO bridge from dashboard → app host
const res = await fetch("/auth/sso-bridge", { method: "POST", credentials: "include" });
const { code } = await res.json();

location.href = `https://app.elizacloud.ai/sso-bridge?code=${encodeURIComponent(code)}`;
```

### Fish Audio streaming TTS (voice)
**[#17709](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17709)** integrates **Fish Audio streaming TTS** into the Cloud voice session pipeline, enabling lower-latency, more natural realtime voice turns.

Operational follow-up that materially improves cold-start voice reliability:
- **Warm every cold cache a realtime turn reads**: **[#17744](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17744)**.
- **Persist interrupted voice turns on the canonical Durable Object path**: **[#17644](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17644)**.

### Gmail as a MESSAGE send connector (Google Workspace)
Two PRs combine into a meaningful new capability:
- **Wire Gmail as a MESSAGE send connector; re-enable “new email” send**: **[#18112](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18112)**  
- **Smart channel routing for `MESSAGE op=send`** (room participant resolution before rolodex; subject param support; email literal targets): **[#18111](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18111)**

Example: sending email through the MESSAGE action (conceptual)
```ts
await runtime.actions.MESSAGE({
  op: "send",
  // Supports email-literal targets after #18111
  to: ["alice@example.com"],
  subject: "Follow-up",
  text: "Thanks for the meeting—here are the notes..."
});
```

### UI: per-connector Settings detail pages (Delegate/Bot lens)
**[#18175](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18175)** migrates Settings → Connectors into per-connector detail pages, improving discoverability and reducing misconfiguration (especially for multi-surface connector deployments).

---

## 3) Bug Fixes (critical + with context)

### Billing auth alternation (50% inference failures) fixed in production
The release promotion **[#17865](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17865)** shipped the fix for an issue where production inference alternated success/failure with “Billing authorization is warming up”. The underlying patch was **[#17745](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17745)**: republish org-balance gate hints after a debit to avoid oscillation.

### Tool-call starvation on reasoning models (planner budget)
**[#17630](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17630)** fixes a failure mode where reasoning models consume the entire completion budget *before emitting* a required tool call. The runtime now widens retries / budgets so `toolChoice: required` doesn’t dead-end mid-reasoning.

### “External-content security envelope” leaking into downstream actions/tools
**[#17629](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17629)** prevents a structural bug where hardened incoming messages were wrapped in-place, and later code that treated `message.content.text` as a plain query/name accidentally carried the entire envelope (markers + payload). This impacted search, skill ops, documents, and app-control surfaces.

### Telegram onboarding continuation secured (browser handoff)
**[#18101](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18101)** addresses a real security gap: browser authentication alone must not bind a Telegram identity. The fix carries a bot-issued opaque continuation through auth and validates Telegram HMAC/freshness server-side before linking.

Related open bug report (still relevant for integrators):  
- **Telegram system-bot onboarding dead / identity not durably bound**: **[#17888](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17888)** (open)

### OAuth success page no longer trusts query params
**[#18065](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18065)** requires verified OAuth markers on `/auth/success` so anonymous navigation cannot render a “Connected” state from query parameters.

### Discord readiness race: message ingress before identity hydration
**[#17645](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17645)** ensures Discord connector waits for “ready identity” before ingesting `messageCreate`, preventing mis-attributed or partial state during startup.

### Reliability of agent memory/recall after latency regression
- **Maximize prompt cache reuse (Cerebras)**: **[#17515](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17515)** reorders prompt composition to improve prefix cache hit rates.
- **Relationships graph builder stale-serve + rolodex bounds**: **[#17876](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17876)** reduces worst-case recall turns (previously measured 33–56s).

---

## 4) API Changes (developer-facing)

### A2A chat boundary: `system` messages are rejected
As of **[#17643](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17643)**, public per-agent A2A endpoints reject caller-authored `system` messages. If you previously injected system directives through A2A, you must migrate to:
- tool calls,
- user/assistant messages, or
- server-attested policy configuration (not caller-authored runtime messages).

### OAuth success proof verification route introduced
**[#18065](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18065)** adds server verification to support `/auth/success` rendering. If you maintain custom OAuth providers, ensure you’re completing the proof step (see updated Cloud worker routes in that PR).

### Managed agent marker consistency
**[#18165](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18165)**: Cloud-managed agents are always marked `ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED`. If your tooling checks this env var to branch behavior (e.g., diagnostics vs managed runtime), this should now be reliable.

---

## 5) Social Media Integrations (Twitter/Telegram/Discord/Farcaster)

### Discord
- Startup/ingress race fixed: **[#17645](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17645)**.
- Secret-scan false positive avoided (readiness diagnostic key composition): **[#17671](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17671)**.

### Telegram
- Secure onboarding continuation: **[#18101](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18101)**.
- Still open (system bot onboarding identity binding + canonical URL concerns): **[#17888](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17888)**.

### Twitter / X
OAuth success hardening impacts Twitter callback surfaces as well (part of **[#18065](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18065)**). If you run the X plugin, verify your callback routes now satisfy the “success-proof” contract and do not rely on client query params.

### Farcaster
No Farcaster-specific PRs/issues were surfaced in this week’s aggregated activity.

---

## 6) Model Provider Updates (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

### OpenAI provider: transient 400 handling + tool-pairing resilience
- Planner rescue lane preserves tool results if the planner dies mid-turn; retries spurious tool-pairing 400s: **[#18180](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18180)**.
- Retry stream-start warming failures in the Cloud SDK path: **[#17875](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17875)** (plugin-elizacloud model wrapper).

### Anthropic + OpenAI: Unicode / “well-formed” sanitization hardening
**[#18096](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18096)** closes sanitizer gaps and updates both Anthropic and OpenAI wire contracts to ensure malformed Unicode does not leak into model requests or planner rendering.

---

## 7) Breaking Changes / V1 → V2 Migration Warnings

### Breaking: A2A no longer accepts caller `system` messages
If you have V1-era integrations that push system policy via message history, you must migrate. Post-change, **A2A treats system policy as a server-controlled boundary**, not caller-supplied content. See **[#17643](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17643)**.

### Potentially breaking: Host-mode routing (apex vs app host)
With **app-mode** (**[#17752](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17752)**), deployments that assume identical behavior across `eliza.app` / `app.elizacloud.ai` may see different routing. If you embed the Cloud UI or run reverse proxies, ensure Host headers are preserved and that your custom domains map intentionally.

### Runtime/CI environment pin: Bun `1.3.14`
The repository is converging on Bun `1.3.14` pins (see **[#17044](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17044)** and **[#17653](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17653)**). If your plugin CI or local dev depends on Bun canary behaviors, expect drift and update accordingly.

---

## Open Issues to Track (high impact)

- Production provisioning failure regression (**16% failure**): **[#18052](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/18052)** (investigate autoscaler maxNodes hardcode, fleet capacity, fence deadlocks, prod daemon pinned behind `main`).
- Login UI blocked by `/steward/auth/providers` latency (up to **4.7s**): **[#18049](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/18049)**.
- Staging E2E job defaults to production Cloud API (coverage defect): **[#18076](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/18076)**.
- Telegram system-bot onboarding identity binding broken: **[#17888](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17888)**.

---

## Developer Discord Notes (context affecting builders)

- The community reiterated that ElizaOS is pivoting to open-source AI agent software and away from token economics. Token governance/control questions remain unresolved in discussion (**2026-08-09** logs). For technical contributors, expect moderation pressure to keep core channels engineering-focused.
- A user asked whether ElizaOS is available on the App Store / iPhone runnable (Discord `#coders`, 2026-08-09). There was no shipping guidance in-thread; if you maintain mobile docs, consider updating the canonical answer in documentation.

# elizaOS Discord - 2026-08-08

## Summary

### Token Status and Project Pivot

The ai16z/ElizaOS project has officially abandoned its token following a class-action lawsuit settlement in early August 2026. Shaw Walters publicly declared the token "dead" after the settlement depleted project resources. The foundation is winding down with no further buybacks or token support planned. This decision came after the project attempted a token rebranding, which was subsequently abandoned months later, leaving token holders without closure. The core team has pivoted to focus exclusively on open-source AI agent software development, completely decoupled from token economics.

### Team Restructuring and Development Philosophy

Shaw Walters explained that during the bull market, the project faced exploitation from opportunistic contributors who joined for financial gain rather than genuine contribution. The team discovered that hiring mercenaries rather than committed builders cost more value than they created. The project has now restructured to a smaller, focused team moving forward without tokens or what Shaw termed "fuckery." Development is reportedly progressing rapidly under this new structure.

Community members expressed significant frustration about the token rebranding followed by abandonment. Token holders are seeking clarity on the token's status, with several users pointing out inconsistencies between promoting a rebranded token and then abandoning it. Some community members threatened legal action over substantial financial losses. The community remains divided on whether the project truly abandoned the token or if there's potential for recovery. Despite these challenges, Shaw acknowledged that many community members lost money and expressed a desire to remedy the situation.

### Ongoing Development and New Interest

Despite the token situation, the underlying open-source AI agent software development continues. New members joined the community expressing interest in building Web3 agent tools. Existing members discussed the broader market recovery. The technical focus has shifted entirely to software development without token economics considerations.

### Community Support and Redemption

In the partners channel, supportive community members acknowledged that Shaw was taken advantage of by others during the project's earlier phases. Long-time followers expressed understanding of the challenges faced and noted satisfaction that things are improving, referencing an ongoing "redemption arc" for the project leadership.
